explanation_excerpt: kbd-new-phase starts things off with a goals file. Then you assess, plan, and execute the changes. At the end you reflect on how it went and figure out what to do next.

gaps.description: Omits the optional analyze stage entirely, and gives no detail on what each stage produces or gates on: assess halts for explicit approval; plan detects OpenSpec; execute runs artifact-refiner QA and archives via verify/archive steps; the closing stage requires ALL changes DONE and passes through the reflector sycophancy gate.
No mention of current-waypoint.json, position-reminder.txt, and progress.json (which must be updated explicitly after each change — never automatic).
No mention of the mandatory progress-signaling protocol (emitting 'Starting'/'Completed' signals with step N of T).

'figure out what to do next' is vague about what the closing stage actually outputs — a structured reflection document with per-goal MET/PARTIAL/NOT MET status, technical debt, lessons, and a recommended next phase.

transfer_problems: A teammate runs the execute stage and, partway through, three changes are marked DONE while two remain IN_PROGRESS. They then invoke the closing/reflection stage directly. What should happen, and why?

A project has an openspec/ directory at its root. During the plan stage, the operator wants to skip OpenSpec and just write changes informally instead. Is this a valid choice, and what breaks if they do it anyway?
